clue.text: For punishment has priest confined regular communicant?

indicators.note: the punishment word is said to have the priest shut up within it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: penal means for or as punishment

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is punished by being locked up by the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communicant' tempts you toward church, but here it is someone who communicates regularly by letter; the question mark flags that pun. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend writes letters on a regular basis, so is jokingly a regular communicator.

clue.text: Remove heart of trendy Docklands area

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, which is taken out

explanation.surface: Gentrification has torn the soul out of a fashionable riverside district.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is a district of East London beside the Docklands.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is a district of East London by the old docks, so an example of a Docklands area.

clue.text: Brown ale flowing round university party

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the university letter
flowing beer moves freely, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Students pour brown ale freely at a campus party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' rearranges BROWN ALE; 'round' puts U inside. Gordon Brown led this rebranded political party, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the 1990s rebranding of the British Labour Party, so a political party.

clue.text: Get up mother with Seventies style, a mixture of elements

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading the pieces from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Mum dresses in a 1970s look that blends several influences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' reverses the whole run MA + GLAM + A; it looks like a costume, 'get-up'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy of mercury with another metal is a blend of chemical elements.

clue.text: Threaten with fury following tip

indicators.note: the fury word comes after the tip word, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: Someone menaces another in a rage after a tip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in danger is to threaten something's safety, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Kiss repeatedly, close together

definitions.meaning: to neck is to kiss, so doing it again and again
level with each other, as in a tight race

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes competitors running level, while literally being kissing over and over.

clue.text: Rushdie topped off account in regular publication

indicators.note: topped means beheaded, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: The novelist is killed off in a story in a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' trims SALMAN to ALMAN. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual reference book appears every year, so it is a regular publication.

clue.text: Leave to set climbing rose

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to put is to set down

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: leave a climbing rose to establish itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower but is the past tense of rise. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose as the past of rise means stood up or got out of bed.

clue.text: Adopt country ways that could make one surreal

indicators.note: the following letters could be made into another word by rearrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Moving to the countryside could make a person feel strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or become rustic is to take on country habits.

clue.text: Exotic fruit makes two servings of pud

indicators.note: two helpings means the word is taken twice over

parts.note: pud is a dialect or nursery word for a hand or paw

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit is enough for two helpings of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pud' looks like pudding, the dessert, but it is the old nursery word for a hand or paw. 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya-like papaw is a tropical fruit, an example of something exotic to eat.

clue.text: Blade and what it could leave round one Cambridge college

indicators.note: the mark left by the blade goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a blade can leave a scar
the Roman numeral I is one
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A sword, and the wound it might inflict, are associated with a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge college' points at the English university, but it is the American Cambridge, home of MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved sword is a kind of blade, so the general word stands for a specific example.

clue.text: Treating again with laser almost complete lack of pain

indicators.note: treating something processes or works it over, so the letters are reworked
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Repeated laser treatment leaves a patient completely free of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LASER to LASE; 'Treating' rearranges AGAIN plus LASE. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for absence of feeling pain is the full insensibility the clue describes.

clue.text: Irregular must escort a troop leader

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Irregular soldiers must accompany a commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troop' suggests soldiers, but a scout troop is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout troop is led by an adult volunteer, the troop's leader.

clue.text: Plane crashed in mountainous country

indicators.note: a crashed plane is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft came down in a mountainous land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom contains Everest, making it the archetypal mountainous country.

clue.text: Contemptible type clubs youngsters without least bit of remorse — one may be sent down here

definitions.text: one may be sent down here

parts.note: a worm is a despicable person
woods are a type of golf club

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the youngsters surround the letter

parts.note: cubs are young animals or junior scouts

indicators.note: the least bit of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A despicable person beats young people, showing not a trace of remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, putting R inside CUBS to make CRUBS. Wormwood Scrubs is a well-known London prison, and being 'sent down' is British slang for being jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent down means being sentenced to prison, and this is a London jail where convicts go.

clue.text: Scramble into group rejecting old surroundings

indicators.note: to scramble is to mix up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to join a group while turning away from their old environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling up one's roots means abandoning a familiar home environment.

clue.text: Widespread disease has holiday region up in terror

indicators.note: the region word is placed inside the terror word
in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: the Med, the Mediterranean, is a popular holiday area

explanation.surface: An outbreak of illness causes terror in a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the holiday region bottom to top, making DEM. 'has' is a link; the surface's resort is just scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease outbreak spread across many countries is the most widespread kind.

clue.text: How chess players compete generally

definitions.meaning: chess players move their pieces over the chequered playing surface
applying to everyone or everything, without exception

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means affecting all levels equally, while literally describing play over a chessboard.

clue.text: Claret's alternatively red

indicators.note: alternatively means in another arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of the word as written, including the final S

explanation.surface: Claret is a kind of red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This bright vivid colour is a shade of red.

clue.text: Method of bowling to give surplus firepower?

parts.note: over means in excess or left over

explanation.surface: A bowling style supposedly delivers extra firepower.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowling here is cricket bowling, delivering the ball with the arm above the shoulder. 'to give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling with the arm swung above the shoulder is the standard cricket delivery method.

clue.text: Holy man in extremely small room in church

indicators.note: the holy man goes inside the word for extremely

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A priest sits in a tiny room in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely small' reads as one phrase, but 'extremely' is VERY and 'small' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where clergy robe and vestments are kept is a small chamber within a church.

clue.text: Detachment from Canada charges Russian retreat

indicators.note: a detachment is a section split off from the following words, so the answer is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A unit from Canada attacks a Russian position that is falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detachment' and 'retreat' suggest a military scene; the answer sits inside canaDA CHArges.
explanation.definitionFit: A country house in Russia is a retreat from the city, so the dacha fits.

clue.text: Beg to get freed finally in prison

indicators.note: the last letter is placed inside the prison word
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prisoner pleads to be released at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge or ask for something free is to beg.

clue.text: Part of skeleton bloke damaged in grip of girl

indicators.note: held in the grip of the girl means placed inside her name
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's bones are injured while a girl holds him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' gives KLEBO; 'in grip of' splits the girl's name around those letters. 'Part of skeleton' reads as a gruesome scene but is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The talus or similar bone at the foot joint is one component of the skeleton.

clue.text: Fellow holding game back — change pitch

indicators.note: the fellow holds the game within him

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion

indicators.note: back means the game word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A man keeps a game going, then switches the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives ODUL. 'pitch' suggests a sports field but means musical tone, and 'game' is the board game, not a match.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, to shift key or vary the tone of the voice is to alter its pitch.

clue.text: American taken in by wet left-winger

indicators.note: the American is taken inside the word for wet

explanation.surface: An American is fooled by a feeble leftist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like British slang for feeble, but simply means damp here.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Chairman Mao is a communist, so very much on the political left.

clue.text: Rear cute hybrid animal

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mix, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone breeds an adorable crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living being, especially an animal, can be called a creature.

clue.text: Singular cat with offensive air

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
moggy is British slang for a cat, especially an ordinary one

explanation.surface: A lone cat has a smelly, unpleasant atmosphere about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' suggests attitude, but means the atmosphere itself, polluted and foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted fog is foul air, so a place full of it has an offensive atmosphere.
